cohort: The study included 108 women with pelvic organ prolapse attending a urogynaecology clinic, 94.7% postmenopausal (mean 65.08 years) and 94.5% parous (mean 4).
finding: The study concluded that risk factors for POP (obesity, hysterectomy, heavy lifting, chronic cough) and the most frequently reported symptoms (stress urinary incontinence and constipation) in this Black population correlated with findings from other studies.
